content.text:
To check how many **new lines** have been added to your project since the last commit, you can use these commands:

### 1. **Quick summary** (shows insertions and deletions per file):
```bash
git diff --stat
```

### 2. **Total new lines added** (uncommitted changes in working directory):
```bash
git diff --numstat | awk '{sum+=$1} END {print "New lines added:", sum}'
```

### 3. **Total new lines added by the last commit** (comparing commit to its parent):
```bash
git diff HEAD~1 --numstat | awk '{sum+=$1} END {print "New lines in last commit:", sum}'
```

### 4. **Count only actual code additions** (excludes blank lines):
```bash
git diff | grep "^+" | grep -v -E "^(\+\+\+|---)" | grep -v "^+$" | wc -l
```

**Most common use case:** If you want to see what you've added since the last commit (uncommitted changes), use option **2**. If you want to see what the last commit itself added, use option **3**.
